after.worked_solution:
Let's rewrite the vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ as a linear combination of the vectors ${q}_{1},{q}_{2},{q}_{3}:$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{q}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{a}_{1} \\ {q}_{2}=\frac{1}{4}{a}_{2}+2{q}_{1} \\ {q}_{3}=\frac{1}{6}{a}_{3}-4{q}_{1}+{q}_{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}=2{q}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}=-8{q}_{1}+4{q}_{2} \\ {a}_{3}=24{q}_{1}-6{q}_{2}+6{q}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, this system can be written in matrix form as follows:

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & {a}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {q}_{1} & {q}_{2} & {q}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 24 \\ 0 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]}}
$$

$$
{r}_{12}+{r}_{22}+{r}_{23}=-8+4+(-6)=-10.
$$

$$

$$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 4 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}}

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained from the columns of $A$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, find  the value of ${q}_{31}\cdot {r}_{12}.$
after.worked_solution:
Let ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ be the columns of $A.$

First, we find an orthonormal basis of $\text{Col}(A)=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**. We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**. We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1}}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-(\frac{4}{2})[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we normalize ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 2\sqrt{2} \\ 0 & \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 2\sqrt{2} \\ 0 & \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Finally, ${q}_{31}\cdot {r}_{12}=(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})\cdot (2\sqrt{2})=-2.$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained from the columns of $A$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, find the value of $\frac{{r}_{22}}{{q}_{12}}.$
after.worked_solution:
Let ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ be the columns of $A.$

First, we find an orthonormal basis of $\text{Col}(A)=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**. We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**. We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1}}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-(-\frac{1}{3})[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+(\frac{1}{3})[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we normalize ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{3}{2\sqrt{6}}[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ 0 & \frac{4}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ 0 & \frac{4}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Finally, $\frac{{r}_{22}}{{q}_{12}}=\frac{(\frac{4}{\sqrt{6}})}{(\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}})}=2.$
